141	d4d_complex_proxy_rubric:
142	  schema_version: "2.0"
143	  description: >
144	    Ten-element hierarchical rubric for evaluating D4D YAML completeness and usability.
145	    Each element represents a complex metadata-driven goal and includes up to five measurable
146	    sub-elements. Scores can be computed at the element or sub-element level.
147	
148	  scoring_scale:
149	    element: 0–5
150	    sub_element: [0, 1]  # 0 = not present/fail, 1 = present/pass
151	
152	  rubric:
153	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
154	    - id: 1
155	      name: "Dataset Discovery and Identification"
156	      description: "Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?"
157	      sub_elements:
158	        - name: "Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)"
159	          field: ["doi", "rrid", "id"]
160	        - name: "Dataset Title and Description Completeness"
161	          field: ["title", "description"]
162	        - name: "Keywords or Tags for Searchability"
163	          field: ["keywords"]
164	        - name: "Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)"
165	          field: ["page", "resources"]
166	        - name: "Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)"
167	          field: ["parent_datasets", "related_datasets"]
168	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
169	
170	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
171	    - id: 2
172	      name: "Dataset Access and Retrieval"
173	      description: "Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?"
174	      sub_elements:
175	        - name: "Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined"
176	          field: ["license_and_use_terms", "ip_restrictions"]
177	        - name: "Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification"
178	          field: ["regulatory_restrictions", "confidentiality_level", "hipaa_compliant", "other_compliance", "governance_committee_contact"]
179	        - name: "Download URL or Platform Link Available"
180	          field: ["download_url"]
181	        - name: "Distribution Formats and File Types Specified"
182	          field: ["distribution_formats", "format", "media_type"]
183	        - name: "Related Datasets and External Resources Linked"
184	          field: ["related_datasets", "external_resources"]
185	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
186	
187	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
188	    - id: 3
189	      name: "Data Reuse and Interoperability"
190	      description: >
191	        Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?
192	
193	        Note: Evaluate whether the dataset is designed for integration with similar datasets,
194	        including: common identifiers for cross-dataset linking, standardized formats for data
195	        harmonization, and documented integration procedures.
196	      sub_elements:
197	        - name: "License Terms Allow Reuse"
198	          field: ["license_and_use_terms"]
199	        - name: "Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)"
200	          field: ["format", "encoding"]
201	        - name: "Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated"
202	          field: ["conforms_to", "conforms_to_schema"]
203	        - name: "Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined"
204	          field: ["variables"]
205	        - name: "Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)"
206	          field: ["intended_uses", "prohibited_uses", "discouraged_uses"]
207	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
208	
209	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
210	    - id: 4
211	      name: "Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards"
212	      description: "Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?"
213	      sub_elements:
214	        - name: "IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact"
215	          field: ["ethical_reviews", "human_subject_research", "data_protection_impacts"]
216	        - name: "Deidentification Method Described"
217	          field: ["is_deidentified"]
218	        - name: "Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment"
219	          field: ["participant_privacy", "reidentification_risk"]
220	        - name: "Informed Consent Obtained from Participants"
221	          field: ["informed_consent"]
222	        - name: "Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented"
223	          field: ["vulnerable_populations", "participant_compensation"]
224	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
225	
226	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
227	    - id: 5
228	      name: "Data Composition and Structure"
229	      description: "Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?"
230	      sub_elements:
231	        - name: "Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described"
232	          field: ["subpopulations"]
233	        - name: "Number of Instances or Samples Reported"
234	          field: ["instances"]
235	        - name: "Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits"
236	          field: ["variables", "is_tabular", "is_data_split", "is_subpopulation"]
237	        - name: "Data Topics or Conditions Represented"
238	          field: ["instances"]
239	        - name: "Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented"
240	          field: ["anomalies", "sampling_strategies", "missing_data_documentation"]
241	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
242	
243	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
244	    - id: 6
245	      name: "Data Provenance and Version Tracking"
246	      description: "Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?"
247	      sub_elements:
248	        - name: "Dataset Version Number Provided"
249	          field: ["version"]
250	        - name: "Version Access Methods Documented"
251	          field: ["version_access"]
252	        - name: "Change Descriptions and Errata Provided"
253	          field: ["errata", "updates"]
254	        - name: "Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated"
255	          field: ["updates"]
256	        - name: "Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources"
257	          field: ["was_derived_from", "release_notes", "raw_data_sources"]
258	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
259	
260	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
261	    - id: 7
262	      name: "Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency"
263	      description: "Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?"
264	      sub_elements:
265	        - name: "Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation"
266	          field: ["purposes"]
267	        - name: "Primary Research Objectives or Tasks"
268	          field: ["tasks"]
269	        - name: "Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed"
270	          field: ["funders"]
271	        - name: "Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present"
272	          field: ["funders"]
273	        - name: "Creators and Acknowledgements Documented"
274	          field: ["creators", "funders"]
275	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
276	
277	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
278	    - id: 8
279	      name: "Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)"
280	      description: >
281	        Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?
282	
283	        Note: Preprocessing and collection metadata may be represented as structured text
284	        descriptions OR as machine-readable provenance graphs (e.g., W3C PROV-O, workflow graphs).
285	        Evaluation should check for: (1) structured text descriptions OR (2) graph representations
286	        with entity-activity-agent relationships. Both formats are acceptable.
287	      sub_elements:
288	        - name: "Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described"
289	          field: ["collection_mechanisms"]
290	        - name: "Data Acquisition Methods Listed"
291	          field: ["acquisition_methods"]
292	        - name: "Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality"
293	          field: ["preprocessing_strategies", "cleaning_strategies", "labeling_strategies", "annotation_analyses", "machine_annotation_tools"]
294	        - name: "Software and Tools Documented"
295	          field: ["software_and_tools"]
296	        - name: "External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols"
297	          field: ["external_resources", "conforms_to", "imputation_protocols"]
298	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
299	
300	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
301	    - id: 9
302	      name: "Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure"
303	      description: "Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?"
304	      sub_elements:
305	        - name: "Known Limitations Documented"
306	          field: ["known_limitations"]
307	        - name: "Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)"
308	          field: ["known_biases"]
309	        - name: "Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted"
310	          field: ["anomalies"]
311	        - name: "Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided"
312	          field: ["sensitive_elements", "content_warnings"]
313	        - name: "Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis"
314	          field: ["ethical_reviews", "future_use_impacts"]
315	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
316	
317	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
318	    - id: 10
319	      name: "Cross-Platform and Community Integration"
320	      description: >
321	        Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?
322	
323	        Note: For Bridge2AI datasets, citation metadata is mandatory and should include:
324	        (1) formatted citation string, (2) DOI, and (3) citation instructions. Hosting
325	        platform identification should specify the publisher or repository (e.g., PhysioNet,
326	        Dataverse, institutional repositories).
327	      sub_elements:
328	        - name: "Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform"
329	          field: ["publisher"]
330	        - name: "Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing"
331	          field: ["citation", "doi"]
332	        - name: "Community Standards or Schema Conformance"
333	          field: ["conforms_to"]
334	        - name: "Outreach Materials and Documentation Links"
335	          field: ["external_resources", "page"]
336	        - name: "Related Datasets with Typed Relationships"
337	          field: ["related_datasets"]
338	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    sub-elements. Scores can be computed at the element or sub-element level.

  scoring_scale:
    element: 0–5
    sub_element: [0, 1]  # 0 = not present/fail, 1 = present/pass

  rubric:
    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 1
      name: "Dataset Discovery and Identification"
      description: "Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)"
          field: ["doi", "rrid", "id"]
        - name: "Dataset Title and Description Completeness"
          field: ["title", "description"]
        - name: "Keywords or Tags for Searchability"
          field: ["keywords"]
        - name: "Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)"
          field: ["page", "resources"]
        - name: "Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)"
          field: ["parent_datasets", "related_datasets"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 2
      name: "Dataset Access and Retrieval"
      description: "Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined"
          field: ["license_and_use_terms", "ip_restrictions"]
        - name: "Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification"
          field: ["regulatory_restrictions", "confidentiality_level", "hipaa_compliant", "other_compliance", "governance_committee_contact"]
        - name: "Download URL or Platform Link Available"
          field: ["download_url"]
        - name: "Distribution Formats and File Types Specified"
          field: ["distribution_formats", "format", "media_type"]
        - name: "Related Datasets and External Resources Linked"
          field: ["related_datasets", "external_resources"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 3
      name: "Data Reuse and Interoperability"
      description: >
        Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

        Note: Evaluate whether the dataset is designed for integration with similar datasets,
        including: common identifiers for cross-dataset linking, standardized formats for data
        harmonization, and documented integration procedures.
      sub_elements:
        - name: "License Terms Allow Reuse"
          field: ["license_and_use_terms"]
        - name: "Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)"
          field: ["format", "encoding"]
        - name: "Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated"
          field: ["conforms_to", "conforms_to_schema"]
        - name: "Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined"
          field: ["variables"]
        - name: "Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)"
          field: ["intended_uses", "prohibited_uses", "discouraged_uses"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 4
      name: "Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards"
      description: "Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact"
          field: ["ethical_reviews", "human_subject_research", "data_protection_impacts"]
        - name: "Deidentification Method Described"
          field: ["is_deidentified"]
        - name: "Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment"
          field: ["participant_privacy", "reidentification_risk"]
        - name: "Informed Consent Obtained from Participants"
          field: ["informed_consent"]
        - name: "Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented"
          field: ["vulnerable_populations", "participant_compensation"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 5
      name: "Data Composition and Structure"
      description: "Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described"
          field: ["subpopulations"]
        - name: "Number of Instances or Samples Reported"
          field: ["instances"]
        - name: "Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits"
          field: ["variables", "is_tabular", "is_data_split", "is_subpopulation"]
        - name: "Data Topics or Conditions Represented"
          field: ["instances"]
        - name: "Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented"
          field: ["anomalies", "sampling_strategies", "missing_data_documentation"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 6
      name: "Data Provenance and Version Tracking"
      description: "Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Dataset Version Number Provided"
          field: ["version"]
        - name: "Version Access Methods Documented"
          field: ["version_access"]
        - name: "Change Descriptions and Errata Provided"
          field: ["errata", "updates"]
        - name: "Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated"
          field: ["updates"]
        - name: "Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources"
          field: ["was_derived_from", "release_notes", "raw_data_sources"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 7
      name: "Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency"
      description: "Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation"
          field: ["purposes"]
        - name: "Primary Research Objectives or Tasks"
          field: ["tasks"]
        - name: "Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed"
          field: ["funders"]
        - name: "Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present"
          field: ["funders"]
        - name: "Creators and Acknowledgements Documented"
          field: ["creators", "funders"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 8
      name: "Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)"
      description: >
        Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

        Note: Preprocessing and collection metadata may be represented as structured text
        descriptions OR as machine-readable provenance graphs (e.g., W3C PROV-O, workflow graphs).
        Evaluation should check for: (1) structured text descriptions OR (2) graph representations
        with entity-activity-agent relationships. Both formats are acceptable.
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described"
          field: ["collection_mechanisms"]
        - name: "Data Acquisition Methods Listed"
          field: ["acquisition_methods"]
        - name: "Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality"
          field: ["preprocessing_strategies", "cleaning_strategies", "labeling_strategies", "annotation_analyses", "machine_annotation_tools"]
        - name: "Software and Tools Documented"
          field: ["software_and_tools"]
        - name: "External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols"
          field: ["external_resources", "conforms_to", "imputation_protocols"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 9
      name: "Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure"
      description: "Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?"
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Known Limitations Documented"
          field: ["known_limitations"]
        - name: "Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)"
          field: ["known_biases"]
        - name: "Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted"
          field: ["anomalies"]
        - name: "Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided"
          field: ["sensitive_elements", "content_warnings"]
        - name: "Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis"
          field: ["ethical_reviews", "future_use_impacts"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
    - id: 10
      name: "Cross-Platform and Community Integration"
      description: >
        Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

        Note: For Bridge2AI datasets, citation metadata is mandatory and should include:
        (1) formatted citation string, (2) DOI, and (3) citation instructions. Hosting
        platform identification should specify the publisher or repository (e.g., PhysioNet,
        Dataverse, institutional repositories).
      sub_elements:
        - name: "Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform"
          field: ["publisher"]
        - name: "Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing"
          field: ["citation", "doi"]
        - name: "Community Standards or Schema Conformance"
          field: ["conforms_to"]
        - name: "Outreach Materials and Documentation Links"
          field: ["external_resources", "page"]
        - name: "Related Datasets with Typed Relationships"
          field: ["related_datasets"]
      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

126	    artifacts on disk: not `label_aware/`, which is where every evaluation
127	    since 2026-08 lives and which the cross-arm table reads, not the dated

159	    counts.update({("kept", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")})
160	    no_schema: Dict[str, int] = {}

162	    kept_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []

166	        shown = eval_file.relative_to(eval_base)

171	        except Exception as e:

177	        if rubric not in schemas:

184	        status, errors = classify(eval_data, schemas[rubric])
185	        counts[(where, status)] += 1
186	        if status == "invalid":
187	            (kept_invalid if where == "kept" else live_invalid).append((shown, errors))
188	        elif status == "superseded":
189	            print(f"🕐 {shown}: superseded shape — {errors[0]}")
190	
191	    for label, rows in (("live", live_invalid), ("kept as evidence", kept_invalid)):
192	        for shown, errors in rows:
193	            print(f"❌ {shown} ({label}):")
194	            for error in errors:
195	                print(f"     {error}")
196	
197	    print()
198	    print("=" * 60)
199	    print("SUMMARY (judged against a schema):")
200	    for where in ("live", "kept"):
201	        row = {k: counts[(where, k)] for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}

210	    # applies, and one kept under an archive marker is evidence of what an
211	    # older instrument produced: reported, never rewritten to pass. Only a
212	    # live invalid artifact fails the run.
213	    return 0 if not live_invalid and not counts[("live", "unreadable")] else 1

216	def cli(argv: List[str] | None = None) -> int:
217	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)

220	    parser.add_argument("--rubric", choices=("rubric10-semantic", "rubric20-semantic"),
221	                        help="require the named outputs to use this rubric")
222	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
223	    if args.rubric and not args.files:
224	        parser.error("--rubric requires --file")
225	    return validate_outputs(args.files, args.rubric) if args.files else main()
226	
227	
228	if __name__ == "__main__":
229	    sys.exit(cli())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Validate D4D evaluation JSON files against their schemas.

This ensures evaluations conform to the standardized schema, which in turn
ensures HTML renderers can reliably parse the output.
"""
import argparse
import json
import re as _re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

try:
    import jsonschema
    from jsonschema import validate, ValidationError
except ImportError:
    print("ERROR: jsonschema package not installed")
    print("Install with: pip install jsonschema")
    sys.exit(1)


def load_schema(schema_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Load JSON Schema file."""
    with open(schema_path, 'r') as f:
        return json.load(f)


def load_evaluation(eval_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Load evaluation JSON file."""
    with open(eval_path, 'r') as f:
        return json.load(f)


#: Top-level keys of the shape that preceded the current agent contract.
#: rubric10 evaluations recorded before 2026 report `summary_scores` and
#: `element_scores`; the agents have instructed `overall_score` and `elements`
#: since. Such a record is not wrong, it is a different vintage — reporting it
#: as invalid buries the records that really are.
SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS = ("summary_scores", "element_scores")


def classify(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
    """Validate, distinguishing a superseded shape from a wrong value.

    Returns `("valid" | "superseded" | "invalid", errors)`.

    The distinction is the point. All 28 recorded evaluations failed before the
    schemas were brought up to the agents (#323), and "Invalid: 28" said nothing
    about which were merely old. Of the 20 that still fail, 12 predate the
    contract and 8 report `max_points: 84` — a maximum the rubric has never had
    (#314). Only the second kind is a defect in a record.
    """
    errors = []
    try:
        validate(instance=eval_data, schema=schema)
        return "valid", []
    except ValidationError as e:
        errors.append(f"Validation error: {e.message}")
        errors.append(f"  Path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.path)}")
        if e.schema_path:
            errors.append(f"  Schema path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.schema_path)}")
        if any(k in eval_data for k in SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS):
            return "superseded", errors
        return "invalid", errors


def validate_evaluation(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[bool, List[str]]:
    """Back-compatible wrapper: superseded records are not valid."""
    status, errors = classify(eval_data, schema)
    return status == "valid", errors


def validate_outputs(paths: List[Path], rubric: str | None = None,
                     schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
    """Require each explicitly named new output to pass its semantic schema.

    Directory names and superseded shapes do not exempt a new output. This
    path reads only the files named by the caller, so an evaluator can check
    its own output without reading another evaluator's judgements (#833).
    """
    schema_dir = schema_dir or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src/download/prompts"
    names = {"rubric10-semantic": "rubric10_semantic_schema.json",
             "rubric20-semantic": "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"}
    failed = not paths
    for path in paths:
        try:
            doc = load_evaluation(path)
            if not isinstance(doc, dict):
                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
            declared = doc.get("rubric")
            if not isinstance(declared, str) or declared not in names:
                raise ValueError(f"no semantic evaluation schema for rubric {declared!r}")
            if rubric is not None and declared != rubric:
                raise ValueError(f"expected {rubric}, found {declared}")
            valid, errors = validate_evaluation(doc, load_schema(schema_dir / names[declared]))
            if not valid:
                raise ValueError("\n".join(errors))
        except (OSError, ValueError, jsonschema.SchemaError) as exc:
            print(f"INVALID {path}: {exc}")
            failed = True
        else:
            print(f"VALID {path}: {declared}")
    return int(failed)


#: A directory whose name marks its contents as kept evidence rather than a
#: live artifact: an archive, a superseded set, or a dated snapshot of one
#: arm's scores. An invalid record in one of these is what an older
#: instrument produced and must not be rewritten to satisfy today's schema,
#: so it is reported and does not fail the run.
KEPT_DIR = _re.compile(r"^(?:_archive|superseded)|^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(?:[_-]|$)")


def is_kept(path: Path, base: Path) -> bool:
    """Is any directory between `base` and `path` an archive marker?"""
    return any(KEPT_DIR.match(part) for part in path.relative_to(base).parts[:-1])


def discover(base: Path) -> List[Path]:
    """Every evaluation JSON under `base`, at any depth.

    The loop was `{rubric}_semantic/concatenated/*.json` — one directory per
    rubric, one level deep (#833). That reached 28 of the 204 semantic
    artifacts on disk: not `label_aware/`, which is where every evaluation
    since 2026-08 lives and which the cross-arm table reads, not the dated
    per-arm subdirectories beside it, and not the archives. The rubric a file
    declares decides which schema it is judged against, so the directory does
    not have to.
    """
    return sorted(base.rglob("*_evaluation.json"))


def main(eval_base: Path | None = None, schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
    """Validate every evaluation JSON under `data/evaluation_llm`.

    The two roots are arguments so that the exit code — the thing #833 asked
    for, and the thing four tests of the helpers did not reach — can be
    exercised end to end over a tree built for the purpose.
    """
    base_dir = Path(__file__).parent.parent
    schema_dir = schema_dir or base_dir / "src" / "download" / "prompts"
    eval_base = eval_base or base_dir / "data" / "evaluation_llm"

    schemas = {
        "rubric10-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric10_semantic_schema.json"),
        "rubric20-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"),
    }

    eval_files = discover(eval_base)
    if not eval_files:
        print(f"No evaluation files found in {eval_base}")
        return 1

    print(f"Found {len(eval_files)} evaluation file(s) under {eval_base}\n")

    counts = {("live", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
    counts.update({("kept", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")})
    no_schema: Dict[str, int] = {}
    live_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []
    kept_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []

    for eval_file in eval_files:
        where = "kept" if is_kept(eval_file, eval_base) else "live"
        shown = eval_file.relative_to(eval_base)
        try:
            eval_data = load_evaluation(eval_file)
            if not isinstance(eval_data, dict):
                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"❌ {shown}: failed to load: {e}")
            counts[(where, "unreadable")] += 1
            continue

        rubric = eval_data.get("rubric", "unknown")
        if rubric not in schemas:
            # Named and counted, not skipped in silence: the presence-style
            # rubric10/rubric20 outputs have no schema in this repository, and
            # a reader of the summary should see that they were not judged.
            no_schema[str(rubric)] = no_schema.get(str(rubric), 0) + 1
            continue

        status, errors = classify(eval_data, schemas[rubric])
        counts[(where, status)] += 1
        if status == "invalid":
            (kept_invalid if where == "kept" else live_invalid).append((shown, errors))
        elif status == "superseded":
            print(f"🕐 {shown}: superseded shape — {errors[0]}")

    for label, rows in (("live", live_invalid), ("kept as evidence", kept_invalid)):
        for shown, errors in rows:
            print(f"❌ {shown} ({label}):")
            for error in errors:
                print(f"     {error}")

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("SUMMARY (judged against a schema):")
    for where in ("live", "kept"):
        row = {k: counts[(where, k)] for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
        print(f"  {where:5}  valid {row['valid']:4}  superseded {row['superseded']:3}  "
              f"invalid {row['invalid']:3}  unreadable {row['unreadable']:3}")
    if no_schema:
        print("  no schema in this repository, not judged: "
              + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(no_schema.items())))
    print("=" * 60)

    # A superseded record is historical output of a contract that no longer
    # applies, and one kept under an archive marker is evidence of what an
    # older instrument produced: reported, never rewritten to pass. Only a
    # live invalid artifact fails the run.
    return 0 if not live_invalid and not counts[("live", "unreadable")] else 1


def cli(argv: List[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--file", type=Path, action="append", dest="files",
                        help="validate this exact new output strictly; repeat for multiple files")
    parser.add_argument("--rubric", choices=("rubric10-semantic", "rubric20-semantic"),
                        help="require the named outputs to use this rubric")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.rubric and not args.files:
        parser.error("--rubric requires --file")
    return validate_outputs(args.files, args.rubric) if args.files else main()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(cli())

282	purposes:
283	- response: >-
284	    To map the spatiotemporal architecture of human cells and use these maps toward the grand
285	    challenge of interpretable genotype-phenotype learning.
286	- response: >-
287	    To deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data,
288	    produced from multimodal interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes and other
289	    proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant
290	    cell lines under perturbed and unperturbed conditions.
291	- response: >-
292	    To stimulate research and development in "visible" machine learning systems that are
293	    informed by multi-scale cell and tissue architecture rather than being black boxes.
294	- response: >-
295	    To produce ethical, AI-ready datasets, packaged with provenance and rich metadata, that
296	    demonstrate FAIR data management and enable transformative biomedical AI research.
297	
298	addressing_gaps:
299	- response: >-
300	    In genomics and precision medicine, machine learning models are often black boxes,
301	    predicting phenotypes from genotypes without an account of the mechanisms by which such
302	    translation occurs. The project addresses this deficiency by generating matched data and
303	    tools that allow models to be built directly on knowledge maps of cell and tissue
304	    architecture.
305	- response: >-
306	    Much of human subcellular architecture remains uncharted, and complementary mapping
307	    technologies have typically been applied separately; the project addresses the absence of
308	    matched, proteome-wide multimodal measurements collected in the same disease-relevant
309	    cellular contexts.
310	- response: >-
311	    The project addresses the absence of an agreed operational definition of AI-readiness for
312	    biomedical data by releasing datasets that are FAIR, provenanced, characterized,
313	    explainable and ethically prepared, licensed and distributed.
314	
315	tasks:
316	- response: >-
317	    Construction of hierarchical, multi-scale maps of human cell architecture, in which each
318	    node is an assembly of proteins in proximity at a given scale, by integrating
319	    protein-protein interaction data and immunofluorescence imaging data.
320	- response: >-
321	    Training and evaluation of visible machine learning systems, including visible neural
322	    networks (VNNs), for interpretable genotype-phenotype prediction.
323	- response: >-
324	    Interpretation of genetic variants and mutations against a structured representation of
325	    cellular components.
326	
327	other_tasks:
328	- task_details: >-
329	    The individual data streams support analyses beyond cell map construction, including
330	    proteome-wide mapping of protein complexes and of differential elution profiles between
331	    control and drug-treated cells, and analysis of transcriptional and fitness phenotypes
332	    from genome-scale CRISPR interference screens.
333	- task_details: >-
334	    The project reports exploring integrative structure modeling of protein communities,
335	    ranking communities by the amount of available structural information from the Protein
336	    Data Bank, the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, crosslinking mass spectrometry and
337	    disorder prediction, and computing integrative structural models of top-ranked communities
338	    using the Integrative Modeling Platform.

589	- mechanism_details: >-
590	    Affinity purification-mass spectrometry on cell lines in which target genes were
591	    endogenously tagged; the project reports tagging 17 genes in MDA-MB-468 with AP-MS
592	    acquired under untreated, paclitaxel and vorinostat conditions, with 34 additional genes
593	    in progress at the time of the preprint.
594	- mechanism_details: >-
595	    Size-exclusion chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (SEC-MS) for proteome-wide
596	    complex and interaction mapping in MDA-MB-468 cells under three conditions and in KOLF2.1J
597	    iPSCs and derivatives.
598	- mechanism_details: >-
599	    Immunofluorescence staining using the Human Protein Atlas resource of antibodies, with
600	    automated fixation and permeabilization protocols implemented on a pipetting robot for the
601	    MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 cell lines, followed by confocal microscopy in four colour channels.
602	- mechanism_details: >-
603	    Single-cell CRISPR screens using a CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors
604	    with 6 guide RNAs per gene, in MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 lines engineered to express inducible
605	    dCas9, read out with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit.
606	
607	collection_timeframes:
608	- timeframe_details: >-
609	    The NIH RePORTER record for the CM4AI Data Generation Project (core project OT2OD032742)
610	    gives a project period of 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31, during which the data in this and other
611	    quarterly releases were generated; no source states a data collection start or end date for
612	    this release.
613	- timeframe_details: >-
614	    The Dataverse record for this release gives a data creation date of 2025-02-27; the
615	    release was published 2026-06-17, with the immunofluorescence image archives published
616	    2026-07-15. The project states that data collection and release continue on a quarterly
617	    basis through the end of the project in November 2026.
618	
619	data_collectors:
620	- collector_details: >-
621	    Lundberg Lab, Stanford University: immunofluorescence-based staining (ICC-IF) and confocal
622	    microscopy producing the spatial proteomics image data.
623	  role: academic_institution
624	- collector_details: >-
625	    Nevan Krogan laboratory, University of California San Francisco: size-exclusion
626	    chromatography-mass spectrometry and affinity purification-mass spectrometry
627	    protein-protein interaction data.
628	  role: academic_institution
629	- collector_details: >-
630	    University of California San Diego: single-cell CRISPR interference perturbation screens
631	    and the MuSIC data integration pipeline. The Dataverse record lists production locations as
632	    University of California San Diego, University of California San Francisco, Stanford
633	    University and University of Virginia.
634	  role: academic_institution
635	- collector_details: >-
636	    University of Virginia: AI-readiness packaging of data, software, metadata and provenance
637	    graphs using the FAIRSCAPE framework, and deposit of the release in the University of
638	    Virginia Dataverse.
639	  role: academic_institution
640	
641	direct_collection:
642	- is_direct: false
643	  collection_details: >-
644	    Data were not collected from individuals. All measurements were made on commercially
645	    available human cell lines: MDA-MB-468 obtained from ATCC and KOLF2.1J iPSCs obtained from
646	    the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative resource. The project describes these
647	    lines as ethically sourced and the resulting data as non-clinical and de-identified.
648	
649	sampling_strategies:
650	- is_sample: true
651	  is_random: false
652	  is_representative: false
653	  strategies: >-
654	    Targeted selection of proteins for multimodal interrogation, initially 100 chromatin
655	    modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac
656	    disorders, subsequently expanded to additional interactors and signaling molecules.
657	    Immunofluorescence imaging of a defined panel of proteins of interest in MDA-MB-468 cells
658	    under each of three treatment conditions. Genome-scale CRISPR interference screening of
659	    11,739 expressed genes in KOLF2.1J iPSCs, and targeted screening of chromatin regulators
660	    with 6 guide RNAs per gene. Selection of two disease-relevant cell lines and a defined
661	    panel of perturbations: MDA-MB-468 untreated or treated with paclitaxel or vorinostat, and
662	    KOLF2.1J iPSCs undifferentiated or differentiated into neural progenitor cells, neurons and
663	    cardiomyocytes.
664	  why_not_representative: >-
665	    Data in this release were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell
666	    lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at
667	    large.
668	  source_caveats: >-
669	    The number of proteins imaged is not stated for the June 2026 release, whose file listing
670	    carries no per-file descriptions. The October 2025 and June 2025 releases describe 464
671	    proteins of interest and the March 2025 release describes 563; the June 2026 image archives
672	    report the same file sizes as the October 2025 ones but different MD5 checksums, so no
673	    count is carried over.
674	
675	preprocessing_strategies:
676	- preprocessing_details: >-
677	    Protein-protein interaction networks are processed using the node2vec deep learning model
678	    to reduce dimensionality, producing a PPI embedding that contains information about each
679	    protein's interactions.
680	  source_caveats: >-
681	    This is a step of the CM4AI Multi-Scale Integrated Cell (MuSIC) pipeline, which consumes
682	    the released input data streams to produce cell maps; the June 2026 release states that
683	    computed cell maps are not included in this release, so this step was not applied to the
684	    artifacts distributed here.
685	- preprocessing_details: >-
686	    Immunofluorescence images are processed using a Human Protein Atlas deep learning model to
687	    reduce dimensionality, producing an image embedding that contains information about protein
688	    localization.
689	  source_caveats: >-
690	    A step of the MuSIC pipeline that produces cell maps; the June 2026 release states that
691	    computed cell maps are not included in this release.
692	- preprocessing_details: >-
693	    The PPI and image embeddings are integrated into a co-embedding for each protein using
694	    contrastive deep learning, so that the original embeddings can be reconstructed with
695	    minimal information loss and proteins with similar PPI and image embeddings receive similar
696	    co-embeddings.
697	  source_caveats: >-
698	    A step of the MuSIC pipeline that produces cell maps; the June 2026 release states that
699	    computed cell maps are not included in this release.
700	- preprocessing_details: >-
701	    Community detection is performed on the all-by-all similarities of pairs of proteins in the
702	    co-embedding space, and the resulting hierarchy of protein communities is output as the
703	    final cell map.
704	  source_caveats: >-
705	    A step of the MuSIC pipeline that produces cell maps; the June 2026 release states that
706	    computed cell maps are not included in this release.
707	
708	cleaning_strategies:
709	- cleaning_details: >-
710	    Each segment of the MuSIC pipeline calls the FAIRSCAPE client package to validate inputs
711	    and to create the output RO-Crate package for that segment, with complete schemas and
712	    validation procedures for all datasets in the provenance graph expressed in JSON-Schema and
713	    resolvable from the package metadata.
714	  source_caveats: >-
715	    Described for the MuSIC pipeline, whose cell map outputs are not included in this release;
716	    the release itself is distributed with RO-Crate metadata and provenance produced by the same
717	    FAIRSCAPE framework.
718	- cleaning_details: >-
719	    Data generated by the acquisition modules undergo quality control before release; the
720	    project preprint records that single-cell CRISPR screen data were being quality controlled
721	    at the time of writing.
722	
723	labeling_strategies:
724	- labeling_details: >-
725	    Cell maps are annotated in a two-pronged approach: first, cell maps are aligned to known
726	    protein function and pathway resources, including the Gene Ontology and Reactome, to
727	    determine protein assemblies with high overlap with known cell biology; second, assemblies
728	    are annotated using a large language model approach that names sets of proteins and assigns
729	    a name confidence score.
730	  source_caveats: >-
731	    This annotation procedure applies to the computed cell maps, which the June 2026 release
732	    states are not included in this release.
733	
734	known_biases:
735	- bias_type: representation_bias
736	  bias_description: >-
737	    Data in this release were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell
738	    lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at
739	    large.
740	  affected_subsets:
741	  - >-
742	    All modalities in the release, which derive from two donor-derived cell lines: MDA-MB-468,
743	    established from a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma, and
744	    KOLF2.1J, derived from a healthy male Northern European donor.
745	- bias_type: selection_bias
746	  bias_description: >-
747	    Proteins and genes were selected for interrogation on the basis of their role as chromatin
748	    modifiers, metabolic enzymes and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric and
749	    cardiac disorders, rather than sampled at random from the proteome; the panels interrogated
750	    by the imaging, interaction and perturbation modalities are targeted rather than
751	    exhaustive.
752	  mitigation_strategy: >-
753	    The perturbation component was extended to an expressed genome-scale CRISPR interference
754	    screen of 11,739 targeted genes in KOLF2.1J iPSCs, broadening coverage beyond the initial
755	    targeted panels.
756	
757	known_limitations:
758	- limitation_type: scope_limitation
759	  limitation_description: >-
760	    This is an interim release. It does not contain predicted cell maps, which will be added in
761	    future releases; the current release is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the
762	    individual datasets.
763	  recommended_mitigation: >-
764	    Users requiring integrated cell maps should await a later quarterly release, or construct
765	    maps from the released input data streams using the Cell Mapping Toolkit.
766	- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
767	  limitation_description: >-
768	    Protein-protein interaction (SEC-MS), protein localization (IF imaging) and CRISPRi
769	    perturb-seq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap.
770	  scope_impact: >-
771	    Analyses requiring all three modalities for the same protein are limited to the
772	    intersection of the three panels.
773	- limitation_type: temporal_limitation
774	  limitation_description: >-
775	    Some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo; in this release the external
776	    perturb-seq links for KOLF2.1J iPSCs and for MDA-MB-468 cells are listed as embargoed.
777	- limitation_type: methodological_limitation
778	  limitation_description: >-
779	    Meaningful analysis of these data requires domain expertise.
780	- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
781	  limitation_description: >-
782	    Immunofluorescence imaging in this release covers only the MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cell
783	    line under the three treatment conditions; the project portal lists iPSC immunofluorescence
784	    images as forthcoming.
785	
786	missing_data_documentation:
787	- missing_data_patterns: >-
788	    Computed cell maps are not included in this release. Protein-protein interaction (SEC-MS),
789	    protein localization (IF imaging) and CRISPRi perturb-seq data interrogate sets of proteins
790	    which incompletely overlap. Perturb-seq external repository links for KOLF2.1J iPSCs and
791	    for MDA-MB-468 cells are listed as embargoed rather than open. AP-MS data are present for
792	    treated MDA-MB-468 cells only; no AP-MS archive is included for the iPSC lines or for
793	    untreated MDA-MB-468 cells in this release.
794	  missing_data_causes: >-
795	    Some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo. The release is an interim Beta
796	    release of an ongoing project whose data acquisition and integration continue through the
797	    end of the project in November 2026.
798	  handling_strategy: >-
799	    The release documents its incompleteness explicitly under a completeness statement, and
800	    commits to regular quarterly updates and augmentation of the dataset through the end of the
801	    project.

808	- use_category: AI model training
809	  usage_notes: >-
810	    The project's stated aim is to enable visible machine learning systems built on knowledge
811	    maps of cell and tissue architecture rather than black-box models.
812	- use_category: Cellular process analysis
813	- use_category: >-
814	    Analysis of cell architectural changes and interactions in the presence of specific disease

# D4D Datasheet for CM4AI Dataset
# Generation Method: schema-grounded agentic, phase 1
# Agent runtime: Claude API (direct)
# Provider: LBL CBORG (proxy to Anthropic)
# Model: claude-opus-5
# Mode: four-phase project agent, generic-v7 prompt
# Prompt: src/download/prompts/d4d_generic_arm_prompt_v7.md (identical for all projects)
# Arm: BASELINE (input documents only)
# Source bundle: data/preprocessed/concatenated/CM4AI_preprocessed.txt
# Source manifest: data/preprocessed/source_manifest.yaml
# Schema: src/data_sheets_schema/schema/data_sheets_schema_all.yaml
# Prior D4D factual reuse: prohibited
# Temperature: 0.0

id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
name: Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)
title: Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)
description: >-
  CM4AI (Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence) is the Functional Genomics Data Generation
  Project of the U.S. National Institutes of Health Bridge2AI program. This record describes
  the June 2026 Data Release (Beta), a multimodal, AI-ready dataset characterizing human cell
  architecture in two disease-relevant cell lines: MDA-MB-468 triple-negative breast cancer
  cells, untreated or treated with paclitaxel or vorinostat, and KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent
  stem cells (iPSCs), undifferentiated or differentiated into neural progenitor cells (NPCs),
  neurons and cardiomyocytes. The release comprises single-cell CRISPR interference
  perturbation sequencing (perturb-seq) for MDA-MB-468 cells with and without treatment and
  for undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs; size-exclusion chromatography-mass spectrometry
  (SEC-MS) protein-protein interaction data for MDA-MB-468 cells with and without treatment
  and for undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs and iPSC-derived NPCs, neurons and cardiomyocytes;
  affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) data for treated MDA-MB-468 cells; and
  immunofluorescence confocal images of protein subcellular localization in MDA-MB-468 cells
  with and without treatment. Data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as
  AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework and are archived in the
  University of Virginia Dataverse. The project's stated objective is to deliver
  machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture, produced by multimodal
  interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes and other proteins involved in
  cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac disorders, in support of interpretable
  genotype-phenotype learning. CM4AI is described as a collaboration of UCSD, UCSF, Stanford,
  UVA, Yale, UT Austin, UA Birmingham, Simon Fraser University and the Hastings Center.

source_caveats: >-
  Referent: this record describes the CM4AI June 2026 Data Release (Beta),
  doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, which the declared source ranking treats as the current release and
  as superseding the October 2025 release. Earlier quarterly releases are recorded under
  related_datasets. Source disagreements resolved here: (1) the CM4AI project portal states
  "Released on: June 17, 2025" for the June 2026 release, while the Dataverse record gives a
  publication date of 2026-06-17; the higher-ranked Dataverse record is preferred. (2) The
  March 2025 release describes immunofluorescence imaging of 563 proteins of interest in
  MDA-MB-468 cells, while the June 2025 and October 2025 releases describe 464; the June 2026
  file listing carries no per-file descriptions, so no protein count is asserted for the image
  archives in this release. (3) The June 2025 release lists NCBI BioProject / Sequence Read
  Archive links for raw perturb-seq sequence data, while the June 2026 release lists the
  corresponding perturb-seq external links as embargoed; the June 2026 statement is preferred.
  (4) The project portal's data-release page marks AP-MS interactomes for the breast cancer
  cells as "coming soon", while the June 2026 Dataverse release includes AP-MS archives for
  paclitaxel- and vorinostat-treated MDA-MB-468 cells; the Dataverse release is preferred.
  Observation on the evidence: the three immunofluorescence image archives in the June 2026
  release report the same file sizes as those in the October 2025 release but different MD5
  checksums, indicating the archives were regenerated; for that reason the per-file protein
  counts stated in the October 2025 descriptions are not carried over. Copyright wording is
  transcribed from the March 2025 release, the most recent release in the bundle that states it
  explicitly; the June 2026 landing page does not restate it. The bundle names no publisher for
  the release and no dataset-level modification date, so `publisher` and `last_updated_on` are
  omitted. Creator affiliations are recorded from the institution names the June 2026 Dataverse
  listing prints for each author; that listing prints a ROR URL rather than an institution name
  for the five University of Virginia authors, and those entries are recorded with the ROR
  identifier. Nine of the 47 listed authors carry no ORCID in the bundle and are recorded with
  fragment identifiers minted on the release DOI, their names and affiliations held in notes.

purposes:
- response: >-
    To map the spatiotemporal architecture of human cells and use these maps toward the grand
    challenge of interpretable genotype-phenotype learning.
- response: >-
    To deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data,
    produced from multimodal interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes and other
    proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant
    cell lines under perturbed and unperturbed conditions.
- response: >-
    To stimulate research and development in "visible" machine learning systems that are
    informed by multi-scale cell and tissue architecture rather than being black boxes.
- response: >-
    To produce ethical, AI-ready datasets, packaged with provenance and rich metadata, that
    demonstrate FAIR data management and enable transformative biomedical AI research.

addressing_gaps:
- response: >-
    In genomics and precision medicine, machine learning models are often black boxes,
    predicting phenotypes from genotypes without an account of the mechanisms by which such
    translation occurs. The project addresses this deficiency by generating matched data and
    tools that allow models to be built directly on knowledge maps of cell and tissue
    architecture.
- response: >-
    Much of human subcellular architecture remains uncharted, and complementary mapping
    technologies have typically been applied separately; the project addresses the absence of
    matched, proteome-wide multimodal measurements collected in the same disease-relevant
    cellular contexts.
- response: >-
    The project addresses the absence of an agreed operational definition of AI-readiness for
    biomedical data by releasing datasets that are FAIR, provenanced, characterized,
    explainable and ethically prepared, licensed and distributed.

tasks:
- response: >-
    Construction of hierarchical, multi-scale maps of human cell architecture, in which each
    node is an assembly of proteins in proximity at a given scale, by integrating
    protein-protein interaction data and immunofluorescence imaging data.
- response: >-
    Training and evaluation of visible machine learning systems, including visible neural
    networks (VNNs), for interpretable genotype-phenotype prediction.
- response: >-
    Interpretation of genetic variants and mutations against a structured representation of
    cellular components.

other_tasks:
- task_details: >-
    The individual data streams support analyses beyond cell map construction, including
    proteome-wide mapping of protein complexes and of differential elution profiles between
    control and drug-treated cells, and analysis of transcriptional and fitness phenotypes
    from genome-scale CRISPR interference screens.
- task_details: >-
    The project reports exploring integrative structure modeling of protein communities,
    ranking communities by the amount of available structural information from the Protein
    Data Bank, the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, crosslinking mass spectrometry and
    disorder prediction, and computing integrative structural models of top-ranked communities
    using the Integrative Modeling Platform.

instances:
- instance_type: >-
    Confocal immunofluorescence image of MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells stained for a protein
    of interest, acquired under untreated, paclitaxel-treated or vorinostat-treated conditions.
    Nuclei are stained with DAPI (blue channel), endoplasmic reticulum with a calreticulin
    antibody (yellow channel), microtubules with a tubulin antibody (red channel) and the
    protein of interest with its antibody (green channel).
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:56
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:15
- instance_type: >-
    Size-exclusion chromatography-mass spectrometry (SEC-MS) protein elution profile used for
    proteome-wide protein complex and interaction mapping, generated for MDA-MB-468 breast
    cancer cells with and without treatment and for undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs and
    iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells, neurons and cardiomyocytes.
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:59
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:28
- instance_type: >-
    Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) protein interaction measurement from
    endogenously tagged bait proteins in paclitaxel- or vorinostat-treated MDA-MB-468 breast
    cancer cells.
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:58
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:26
- instance_type: >-
    Single-cell transcriptome from a CRISPR interference perturbation screen (perturb-seq),
    associated with a targeted gene; the KOLF2.1J iPSC perturbation cell atlas maps
    transcriptional and fitness phenotypes associated with 11,739 targeted genes, and
    perturb-seq data are also provided for MDA-MB-468 cells with and without treatment.
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:64
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:12
