- source_description: >-
    MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419), a triple negative breast cancer cell line established from a
    metastatic site pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary
    adenocarcinoma. The project states the line has been extensively used to study
    triple-negative breast cancer and is well characterized, with transcriptomic, mutational
    profile and whole-genome sequencing data available.
  source_type: Commercially available human cancer cell line
  access_details: Available from ATCC.
- source_description: >-
    KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3), an induced pluripotent stem cell line derived from a healthy
    male Northern European donor, used undifferentiated and differentiated into neural
    progenitor cells, neurons and cardiomyocytes.
  source_type: Human induced pluripotent stem cell line
  access_details: >-
    Available from the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative (HipSci) resource, and
    available for access by non-for-profit organizations via a simple MTA.
- source_description: >-
    Raw mass spectrometry files underlying the SEC-MS and AP-MS archives in this release.
  source_type: Repository deposit
  raw_data_format: Mass spectrometry raw data files
  access_details: >-
    Deposited in the MassIVE repository; separate deposits are listed for SEC-MS in KOLF2.1J
    iPSCs and derivatives, SEC-MS in MDA-MB-468 cells, and AP-MS in paclitaxel-treated and
    vorinostat-treated MDA-MB-468 cells.
- source_description: >-
    Raw single-cell sequence data underlying the genome-scale CRISPR interference perturbation
    cell atlas in KOLF2.1J iPSCs and the perturb-seq data in MDA-MB-468 cells.
  source_type: Repository deposit
  raw_data_format: Single-cell RNA sequencing raw sequence data
  access_details: >-
    The June 2026 release lists the external perturb-seq links for both KOLF2.1J iPSCs and
    MDA-MB-468 cells as embargoed; a raw sequence archive record is included in the release
    itself.

acquisition_methods:
- acquisition_details: >-
    Protein-protein interactions measured by affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS)
    on endogenously tagged cell lines.
  was_directly_observed: true
  was_reported_by_subjects: false
- acquisition_details: >-
    Proteome-wide protein complex and interaction profiles measured by size-exclusion
    chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (SEC-MS), used as an orthogonal mass
    spectrometry-based approach to AP-MS.
  was_directly_observed: true
  was_reported_by_subjects: false
- acquisition_details: >-
    Protein subcellular localization observed by immunofluorescence-based staining (ICC-IF)
    using Human Protein Atlas antibodies followed by confocal microscopy.
  was_directly_observed: true
  was_reported_by_subjects: false
- acquisition_details: >-
    Transcriptional and fitness phenotypes observed in single-cell CRISPR interference
    perturbation screens.
  was_directly_observed: true
  was_reported_by_subjects: false

collection_mechanisms:
- mechanism_details: >-
    Affinity purification-mass spectrometry on cell lines in which target genes were
    endogenously tagged; the project reports tagging 17 genes in MDA-MB-468 with AP-MS
    acquired under untreated, paclitaxel and vorinostat conditions, with 34 additional genes
    in progress at the time of the preprint.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Size-exclusion chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (SEC-MS) for proteome-wide
    complex and interaction mapping in MDA-MB-468 cells under three conditions and in KOLF2.1J
    iPSCs and derivatives.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Immunofluorescence staining using the Human Protein Atlas resource of antibodies, with
    automated fixation and permeabilization protocols implemented on a pipetting robot for the
    MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 cell lines, followed by confocal microscopy in four colour channels.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Single-cell CRISPR screens using a CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors
    with 6 guide RNAs per gene, in MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 lines engineered to express inducible
    dCas9, read out with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit.

collection_timeframes:
- timeframe_details: >-
    The NIH RePORTER record for the CM4AI Data Generation Project (core project OT2OD032742)
    gives a project period of 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31, during which the data in this and other
    quarterly releases were generated; no source states a data collection start or end date for
    this release.
- timeframe_details: >-
    The Dataverse record for this release gives a data creation date of 2025-02-27; the
    release was published 2026-06-17, with the immunofluorescence image archives published
    2026-07-15. The project states that data collection and release continue on a quarterly
    basis through the end of the project in November 2026.

data_collectors:
- collector_details: >-
    Lundberg Lab, Stanford University: immunofluorescence-based staining (ICC-IF) and confocal
    microscopy producing the spatial proteomics image data.
  role: academic_institution
- collector_details: >-
    Nevan Krogan laboratory, University of California San Francisco: size-exclusion
    chromatography-mass spectrometry and affinity purification-mass spectrometry
    protein-protein interaction data.
  role: academic_institution
- collector_details: >-
    University of California San Diego: single-cell CRISPR interference perturbation screens
    and the MuSIC data integration pipeline. The Dataverse record lists production locations as
    University of California San Diego, University of California San Francisco, Stanford
    University and University of Virginia.
  role: academic_institution
- collector_details: >-
    University of Virginia: AI-readiness packaging of data, software, metadata and provenance
    graphs using the FAIRSCAPE framework, and deposit of the release in the University of
    Virginia Dataverse.
  role: academic_institution

direct_collection:
- is_direct: false
  collection_details: >-
    Data were not collected from individuals. All measurements were made on commercially
    available human cell lines: MDA-MB-468 obtained from ATCC and KOLF2.1J iPSCs obtained from
    the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative resource. The project describes these
    lines as ethically sourced and the resulting data as non-clinical and de-identified.

sampling_strategies:
- is_sample: true
  is_random: false
  is_representative: false
  strategies: >-
    Targeted selection of proteins for multimodal interrogation, initially 100 chromatin
    modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac
    disorders, subsequently expanded to additional interactors and signaling molecules.
    Immunofluorescence imaging of a defined panel of proteins of interest in MDA-MB-468 cells
    under each of three treatment conditions. Genome-scale CRISPR interference screening of
    11,739 expressed genes in KOLF2.1J iPSCs, and targeted screening of chromatin regulators
    with 6 guide RNAs per gene. Selection of two disease-relevant cell lines and a defined
    panel of perturbations: MDA-MB-468 untreated or treated with paclitaxel or vorinostat, and
    KOLF2.1J iPSCs undifferentiated or differentiated into neural progenitor cells, neurons and
    cardiomyocytes.
  why_not_representative: >-
    Data in this release were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell
    lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at
    large.
  source_caveats: >-
    The number of proteins imaged is not stated for the June 2026 release, whose file listing
    carries no per-file descriptions. The October 2025 and June 2025 releases describe 464
    proteins of interest and the March 2025 release describes 563; the June 2026 image archives
    report the same file sizes as the October 2025 ones but different MD5 checksums, so no
    count is carried over.

preprocessing_strategies:
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Protein-protein interaction networks are processed using the node2vec deep learning model
    to reduce dimensionality, producing a PPI embedding that contains information about each
    protein's interactions.
  source_caveats: >-
    This is a step of the CM4AI Multi-Scale Integrated Cell (MuSIC) pipeline, which consumes
    the released input data streams to produce cell maps; the June 2026 release states that
    computed cell maps are not included in this release, so this step was not applied to the
    artifacts distributed here.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Immunofluorescence images are processed using a Human Protein Atlas deep learning model to
    reduce dimensionality, producing an image embedding that contains information about protein
    localization.
  source_caveats: >-
    A step of the MuSIC pipeline that produces cell maps; the June 2026 release states that
    computed cell maps are not included in this release.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    The PPI and image embeddings are integrated into a co-embedding for each protein using
    contrastive deep learning, so that the original embeddings can be reconstructed with
    minimal information loss and proteins with similar PPI and image embeddings receive similar
    co-embeddings.
  source_caveats: >-
    A step of the MuSIC pipeline that produces cell maps; the June 2026 release states that
    computed cell maps are not included in this release.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Community detection is performed on the all-by-all similarities of pairs of proteins in the
    co-embedding space, and the resulting hierarchy of protein communities is output as the
    final cell map.
  source_caveats: >-
    A step of the MuSIC pipeline that produces cell maps; the June 2026 release states that
    computed cell maps are not included in this release.

cleaning_strategies:
- cleaning_details: >-
    Each segment of the MuSIC pipeline calls the FAIRSCAPE client package to validate inputs
    and to create the output RO-Crate package for that segment, with complete schemas and
    validation procedures for all datasets in the provenance graph expressed in JSON-Schema and
    resolvable from the package metadata.
  source_caveats: >-
    Described for the MuSIC pipeline, whose cell map outputs are not included in this release;
    the release itself is distributed with RO-Crate metadata and provenance produced by the same
    FAIRSCAPE framework.
- cleaning_details: >-
    Data generated by the acquisition modules undergo quality control before release; the
    project preprint records that single-cell CRISPR screen data were being quality controlled
    at the time of writing.

labeling_strategies:
- labeling_details: >-
    Cell maps are annotated in a two-pronged approach: first, cell maps are aligned to known
    protein function and pathway resources, including the Gene Ontology and Reactome, to
    determine protein assemblies with high overlap with known cell biology; second, assemblies
    are annotated using a large language model approach that names sets of proteins and assigns
    a name confidence score.
  source_caveats: >-
    This annotation procedure applies to the computed cell maps, which the June 2026 release
    states are not included in this release.

known_biases:
- bias_type: representation_bias
  bias_description: >-
    Data in this release were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell
    lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at
    large.
  affected_subsets:
  - >-
    All modalities in the release, which derive from two donor-derived cell lines: MDA-MB-468,
    established from a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma, and
    KOLF2.1J, derived from a healthy male Northern European donor.
- bias_type: selection_bias
  bias_description: >-
    Proteins and genes were selected for interrogation on the basis of their role as chromatin
    modifiers, metabolic enzymes and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric and
    cardiac disorders, rather than sampled at random from the proteome; the panels interrogated
    by the imaging, interaction and perturbation modalities are targeted rather than
    exhaustive.
  mitigation_strategy: >-
    The perturbation component was extended to an expressed genome-scale CRISPR interference
    screen of 11,739 targeted genes in KOLF2.1J iPSCs, broadening coverage beyond the initial
    targeted panels.

known_limitations:
- limitation_type: scope_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    This is an interim release. It does not contain predicted cell maps, which will be added in
    future releases; the current release is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the
    individual datasets.
  recommended_mitigation: >-
    Users requiring integrated cell maps should await a later quarterly release, or construct
    maps from the released input data streams using the Cell Mapping Toolkit.
- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Protein-protein interaction (SEC-MS), protein localization (IF imaging) and CRISPRi
    perturb-seq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap.
  scope_impact: >-
    Analyses requiring all three modalities for the same protein are limited to the
    intersection of the three panels.
- limitation_type: temporal_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo; in this release the external
    perturb-seq links for KOLF2.1J iPSCs and for MDA-MB-468 cells are listed as embargoed.
- limitation_type: methodological_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Meaningful analysis of these data requires domain expertise.
- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Immunofluorescence imaging in this release covers only the MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cell
    line under the three treatment conditions; the project portal lists iPSC immunofluorescence
    images as forthcoming.

missing_data_documentation:
- missing_data_patterns: >-
    Computed cell maps are not included in this release. Protein-protein interaction (SEC-MS),
    protein localization (IF imaging) and CRISPRi perturb-seq data interrogate sets of proteins
    which incompletely overlap. Perturb-seq external repository links for KOLF2.1J iPSCs and
    for MDA-MB-468 cells are listed as embargoed rather than open. AP-MS data are present for
    treated MDA-MB-468 cells only; no AP-MS archive is included for the iPSC lines or for
    untreated MDA-MB-468 cells in this release.
  missing_data_causes: >-
    Some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo. The release is an interim Beta
    release of an ongoing project whose data acquisition and integration continue through the
    end of the project in November 2026.
  handling_strategy: >-
    The release documents its incompleteness explicitly under a completeness statement, and
    commits to regular quarterly updates and augmentation of the dataset through the end of the
    project.

intended_uses:
- use_category: AI-ready datasets to support research in functional genomics
  usage_notes: >-
    The datasets are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata in RO-Crate format so
    that inputs, computations, software and outputs are machine-resolvable.
- use_category: AI model training
  usage_notes: >-
    The project's stated aim is to enable visible machine learning systems built on knowledge
    maps of cell and tissue architecture rather than black-box models.
- use_category: Cellular process analysis
- use_category: >-
    Analysis of cell architectural changes and interactions in the presence of specific disease
    processes, treatment conditions, or genetic perturbations
  usage_notes: >-
    The release pairs untreated and drug-treated breast cancer cells and undifferentiated and
    differentiated iPSCs to support comparison across conditions and cell types.

discouraged_uses:
- discouragement_details: >-
    Use of this interim release for analyses that require integrated, computed cell maps is
    discouraged, because cell maps are not included and will be added in future releases; the
    current release is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets.
- discouragement_details: >-
    Analysis without relevant domain expertise is discouraged; the release states that
    meaningful analysis requires domain expertise.
- discouragement_details: >-
    Generalization from these data to the population at large is discouraged, since the data
    derive from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all
    biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.

prohibited_uses:
- prohibition_reason: >-
    These laboratory data are not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context
    involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval.
- prohibition_reason: >-
    Commercial use is not permitted under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license; commercial use requires
    a separate license negotiation with the copyright holder (UCSD, Stanford, and/or UCSF
    depending upon the specific data package in question), supervised by the Data Access
    Committee.
- prohibition_reason: >-
    Redistribution of adapted material under terms other than the same CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license,
    or with additional legal or technological measures that restrict what the license permits,
    is not allowed.

future_use_impacts:
- impact_details: >-
    Because the data derive from two commercially available de-identified human cell lines and
    do not represent all biological variants seen in the population at large, models trained on
    them may not generalize across donors, populations or cellular contexts.
- impact_details: >-
    The project's Ethics module anticipates potential applications of the data and derived AI
    and machine learning systems and integrates them into data governance frameworks in order
    to optimize benefits, mitigate potential risks and promote use for the collective good; it
    is developing guidelines, a value repository, a CM4AI Life Cycle framework of governance
    milestones and tools to support awareness of the ethical, legal and social ramifications of
    the data and consequent AI systems.
- impact_details: >-
    Applying these laboratory data in clinical or patient-care settings without appropriate
    regulatory oversight and approval is identified by the data generators as a foreseeable
    misuse.

license_and_use_terms:
  license_terms: >-
    Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0),
    https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/. Users are free to share and adapt the
    material provided they give appropriate credit, provide a link to the license and indicate
    if changes were made; may not use the material for commercial purposes; must distribute
    contributions built on the material under the same license; and may not apply legal terms
    or technological measures that legally restrict others from doing anything the license
    permits. Attribution is required to the copyright holders and to the Cell Maps for
    Artificial Intelligence project, and any publications referencing this data or derived
    products should cite the related publication as well as directly citing this data
    collection. Commercial use requires a separate license negotiation with the copyright
    holder (UCSD, Stanford, and/or UCSF depending upon the specific data package in question).
  data_use_permission: no_commercial_use
  notes: >-
    The Dataverse record adds that community norms and good scientific practices expect proper
    credit to be given via citation, using the data citation shown on the dataset page. No
    source names a contact person for license or use terms; commercial licensing is directed to
    the copyright holder.

ip_restrictions:
  restrictions:
  - >-
    Copyright to the datasets is held by the Regents of the University of California except
    where otherwise indicated.
  - >-
    Raw image data for spatial proteomics is copyright by The Board of Trustees of the Leland
    Stanford Junior University.
  - >-
    The ShareAlike condition requires that remixed, transformed or built-upon material be
    distributed under the same license as the original.
  - >-
    Commercial use requires a separate license negotiation with the copyright holder (UCSD,
    Stanford, and/or UCSF depending upon the specific data package in question); a Data Access
    Committee supervises ethical matters related to dataset distribution and potential dual
    licensing for commercial use.
  source_caveats: >-
    The copyright wording is transcribed from the March 2025 release, which states it
    explicitly; the June 2026 landing page does not restate the copyright holders. The project
    preprint states the same allocation of copyright between the University of California and
    Stanford University.

regulatory_restrictions:
  confidentiality_level: unrestricted
  regulatory_restrictions:
  - >-
    The release states that the dataset does not involve human subjects, that samples are
    de-identified, and that the data are not FDA regulated.
  - >-
    Use of these laboratory data in clinical decision-making or in any context involving
    patient care requires appropriate regulatory oversight and approval.
  other_compliance: >-
    The project states that its datasets comply with the FAIR Principles for data and software,
    an NIH requirement, and that ethical conditions of release include full documentation of
    scientific methods and reagents and licensing and distribution open to the scientific
    community for reuse. The release names Jillian Parker (jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu) as
    the Data Governance Committee contact.

data_governance:
  access_review_process: >-
    All files in the release are publicly accessible from the University of Virginia Dataverse
    under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; no access request is required for the published files. The project
    preprint states that a Data Access Committee will supervise ethical matters related to
    dataset distribution and potential dual licensing for commercial use, and that requests for
    commercial use are handled through separate license negotiation with the copyright holder.
  stewardship_roles:
  - >-
    Data Governance Committee contact for the release: Jillian Parker
    (jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu), University of California San Diego.
  - >-
    Ethical review contacts for the release: Vardit Ravitsky
    (ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon
    (jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca).
  - >-
    Point of contact for the dataset: Trey Ideker, University of California San Diego.
  - >-
    Program management: Swathi Thaker, PhD, University of Alabama at Birmingham
    (snthaker@uab.edu).
  - >-
    Archival stewardship: University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), which commits to long
    term preservation supported by committed institutional funds.
  notes: >-
    The project also reports that its Ethics team worked with the Data Acquisition, Tools and
    Standards modules on a plan for ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination and data
    access supervision, balancing openness of the data with protection of intellectual property
    and supervision of potential commercialization, and that a Bridge2AI Code of Conduct
    governs participants accessing Bridge2AI data including CM4AI datasets.
  source_caveats: >-
    Two differently named bodies appear in the bundle and are not equated by any source: the
    June 2026 release names a "Data Governance Committee" contact, while the May 2024 preprint
    states in the future tense that "A Data Access Committee will supervise ethical matters
    related to dataset distribution and potential dual licensing for commercial use" without
    naming it or its members. No committee name, membership or contact identifier is asserted
    here; the named individuals are recorded under stewardship_roles in the roles the sources
    give them.

ethical_reviews:
- review_details: >-
    The release states that the dataset does not involve human subjects, that samples are
    de-identified, and that the data are not FDA regulated, and names Vardit Ravitsky and
    Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon as ethical review contacts. The CM4AI Ethics module developed
    guidelines and best practices for the ethical development of AI systems leveraging this
    data, using a methodology inspired by Value-Sensitive Design to create normative standards
    and expectations, an axiological repository of values, and a CM4AI Life Cycle framework
    elucidating governance milestones throughout data generation and AI system development. It
    also conducts mixed qualitative and quantitative empirical research to capture community
    insights and is developing tools to support awareness of the ethical, legal and social
    ramifications of the data and consequent AI systems.
  reviewing_organization: CM4AI Ethics module
  contact_person: ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801

human_subject_research:
  involves_human_subjects: false
  regulatory_compliance:
  - >-
    The release states: Human Subjects: No; De-identified Samples: Yes; FDA Regulated: No. The
    project preprint states that CM4AI data are distinctive within Bridge2AI in being
    non-clinical, derived from tissue cultures, and considered de-identified as they cannot be
    matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.
  ethics_review_board: >-
    Ethical oversight is provided through the CM4AI Ethics module, with review contacts Vardit
    Ravitsky and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon; no institutional review board approval is
    recorded for the release, consistent with its statement that no human subjects are
    involved.

is_deidentified:
  identifiable_elements_present: false
  deidentification_details: >-
    The release states that samples are de-identified. All data derive from commercially
    available human cell lines, MDA-MB-468 obtained from ATCC and KOLF2.1J iPSCs from the Human
    Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative resource. The project states that such data are
    non-clinical and are considered de-identified because they cannot be matched, with current
    knowledge, to a human subject.

sensitive_elements:
- sensitive_elements_present: false
  sensitivity_details: >-
    The release records no human subjects and de-identified samples; the released content
    consists of laboratory measurements on commercially available human cell lines
    (immunofluorescence images, mass spectrometry-derived interaction data and single-cell
    sequencing summaries) rather than personal identifiers or protected health information.

updates:
  frequency: Quarterly
  update_details: >-
    The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in
    November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis. CM4AI delivers machine-readable
    hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data together with quarterly data
    releases of map-input data streams; each quarterly release is deposited as a separately
    versioned dataset with its own DOI in the University of Virginia Dataverse. Future releases
    are stated to add computed cell maps, iPSC immunofluorescence images, and further AP-MS
    interactomes.

retention_limit:
  retention_details: >-
    Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse, supported by committed
    institutional funds. Files are not removed from previously published versions of a dataset,
    and prior quarterly releases remain available in the same Dataverse collection.

version_access:
  latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
  versions_available:
  - 'Version 2.0 (current): June 2026 Data Release (Beta), doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'
  - 'October 2025 Data Release (Beta), Version 2.1, doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM'
  - 'June 2025 Data Release (Beta), Version 2.1, doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R'
  - 'March 2025 Data Release (Beta), Version 1.4, doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX'
  - 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - Data Release, doi:10.18130/V3/DXWOS5'
  version_details: >-
    Quarterly releases are published as separate Dataverse datasets, each with its own DOI and
    its own internal version history; within a release, minor and major version updates are
    recorded by the repository and files are not removed from previously published versions.
    Software packages used to produce each release are versioned, and the version used to
    produce a dataset is referenced in that dataset's metadata.

content.text:
Validation passed with exit status 0.

## Definition check

The section headed "Source rubric and schema paths (#158)" is present in my instructions. The sentence beginning "Read release-specific notes" reads, verbatim and in full:

> Read release-specific notes from the dedicated `updates.update_details` field, `updates.description` or `notes`, requiring actual release or derivation information rather than crediting unrelated notes.

This matches the current rules (it names the dedicated `updates.update_details` field rather than an absent top-level `release_notes` slot), so I proceeded. The record's `updates.update_details` and `notes` did carry actual release/derivation information, which is what I credited under Element 6.

## Result

**42 / 47 adjusted (89.4%) · 42 / 50 fixed (84.0%) · 3 sub-elements N/A**

| El | Score | El | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Discovery | 5/5 | 6 Provenance | 5/5 |
| 2 Access | 5/5 | 7 Motivation/Funding | 5/5 |
| 3 Reuse | 4/5 | 8 Technical Transparency | 3/5 |
| 4 Ethics | 2/**2** | 9 Limitations | 4/5 |
| 5 Composition | 4/5 | 10 Integration | 5/5 |

**Element 4 applicability (#1060).** Resolved per sub-element on evidence outside E4. The human-subjects condition plainly fails — `description`/`keywords` name MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J cell lines with no participant or clinical terms, `collection_mechanisms` describe assays not recruitment, and `direct_collection.is_direct: false` states "Data were not collected from individuals." So 4.3–4.5 are `applicable: false`, `score: null`, denominator 47. The governance disjunct does succeed for 4.1–4.2 on E2 evidence: `regulatory_restrictions` state an *applying* constraint (clinical use requires regulatory oversight) and `other_compliance` names a Data Governance Committee contact, over donor-derived material — the paradigm case the instrument describes. Both scored 1.

**The two zeros that matter most.** E8.3 and E8.4 fail for a reason the record itself supplies: six `source_caveats` state that the preprocessing and labeling entries describe the MuSIC pipeline whose cell maps are *not in this release*, one saying the step "was not applied to the artifacts distributed here." Three of five `file_collections` are typed `processed_data`, so the released archives were processed — but nothing says how, and no software is named in a producing or transforming role. What is named falls into excluded roles (c)/(d) FAIRSCAPE packaging and validation, (b) Dataverse hosting, (a) the 10x capture kit, (e) MuSIC/Cell Mapping Toolkit/IMP. The candour is creditable and is what made the gap diagnosable; it does not fill it.

Other zeros: `variables` absent entirely (3.4, 5.3) and `anomalies` absent (9.3).

Seven borderline calls resolved to 1 — absent `download_url`, container-only formats, no formal deidentification method, empty `subpopulations`, thin instance counts, no `errata`, omitted `publisher` — each scored on the sub-element's "Look for" scope with the slot omission recorded as a flagged issue rather than silently credited. Correctness validations all passed: DOI prefix 10.18130 coheres with the UVA Dataverse host and citation, four NIH award numbers parse correctly, RRIDs/ORCIDs/RORs well-formed, file counts sum to the declared total. Three consistency failures, twelve warnings.

Output at `output_evaluation.json`, with `instrument_sha256` `66ad6231…`, `instrument_kind: agent_definition`, `temperature: null`, and `claude-opus-5` as both `name` and `evaluator_model`.
